message.content:
Context: we are verifying Ali Nourai's "An Etymological Dictionary of Persian, English and other Indo-European Languages" (1999). Nourai cites 117 references by 3-letter abbreviation plus page number (e.g. KLN:164). We need to find full-text online copies of these references so that later agents can check the exact cited page.

Files:
- Bibliography (OCR text of the book's Tables III and IV, listing every abbreviation with author/title/year): /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sfmqrb-git-rishe/b3fc9033-a4ae-4052-ab02-8a5f609ee6da/scratchpad/bibliography_raw.txt
- Citation counts per abbreviation: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sfmqrb-git-rishe/b3fc9033-a4ae-4052-ab02-8a5f609ee6da/scratchpad/ref_counts.txt

YOUR SHARE: the Western-language references (English, German, French, Latin-script scholarship), i.e. these abbreviations:
AHD POK KLN HRN IEC KNT SYN WLD ISS OEW HUB BRT FSD SKT PRT NYB HJB PHN LKT WEB SIN AHM CEL GPL MAG DEV DRM ZAW SLW BLY KGW SHP AID OXF MPP DVS SPG PHD TYL LAM UNV LAT NAT TTS DOZ AVG LEW SDQ ROE AFA FWE MFL TLM BST HID AIN ZAP AWH ARP EAV PEI SOG LST PLA AKD RCH
(Another agent handles the Persian/Arabic-language references.)

For EACH abbreviation, in order of citation count (most-cited first — AHD, POK, KLN, HRN, IEC, KNT, SYN matter most), find the best online full-text copy:
1. archive.org: use the search API, e.g.
   curl -s 'https://archive.org/advancedsearch.php?q=<query>&fl[]=identifier&fl[]=title&fl[]=year&rows=20&output=json'
   then check https://archive.org/metadata/<identifier> for a file ending in `_djvu.txt` (the OCR text). Prefer the edition Nourai cites (his page numbers refer to that edition; note the edition/year you found if it differs). Note that many scans have "restricted" access (lending library) — the djvu.txt may still be downloadable; test with `curl -sI https://archive.org/download/<id>/<file>_djvu.txt` and record the HTTP status.
2. If found, DOWNLOAD the djvu.txt to /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sfmqrb-git-rishe/b3fc9033-a4ae-4052-ab02-8a5f609ee6da/scratchpad/refs/<ABBR>.txt (curl -L). Then figure out the mapping between the book's printed page numbers and the OCR text: the djvu text has no page markers except form-feeds (\f) between pages, so find a printed page number in the text near a known entry and record the offset (e.g. "printed page N = form-feed page N+14"). Record this as `page_offset` (may be approximate). Also record how entries look (e.g. Klein: headword in bold caps at line start) so a grep strategy works.
3. Otherwise check: Google Books full view, HathiTrust full view (babel.hathitrust.org), titus.uni-frankfurt.de (Bartholomae AiW, Pokorny), indo-european.info / starlingdb.org (Pokorny), ahdictionary.com (AHD IE appendix, online), parsig.org / archive.org (MacKenzie Pahlavi), etymonline, Perseus, dsal.uchicago.edu (Platts, Steingass), archive.org for Hobson-Jobson, Laufer's Sino-Iranica, Skeat, Partridge, Nyberg, Kent's Old Persian (available at archive.org), Buck's Synonyms, Mann's IEC, Walde-Pokorny, Hübschmann, Horn, Lokotsch, Jeffery's Foreign Vocabulary of the Qur'an, Bailey's Khotanese texts, etc. Record the URL and how to look a word up (URL pattern).
4. If genuinely nothing is online, say `none` and note what you tried.

Use Bash curl for archive.org APIs and downloads; use WebSearch/WebFetch for discovery. Do not spend more than ~5 minutes on any single obscure reference cited fewer than 5 times.

OUTPUT: write /tmp/claude-1000/-home-sfmqrb-git-rishe/b3fc9033-a4ae-4052-ab02-8a5f609ee6da/scratchpad/refs_online_western.json as a JSON object keyed by abbreviation:
{"KLN": {"title": "...", "edition_found": "1966/1971", "kind": "archive_djvu|website|google_books|hathitrust|none", "url": "...", "identifier": "...", "local_file": "/…/refs/KLN.txt" or null, "page_offset": "printed p = djvu page +N" or null, "lookup_hint": "how to find an entry / URL pattern", "notes": "..."}, ...}
Validate with python3 -m json.tool. Reply with a short summary: which references were found (with kind), which were not, and total size of downloaded text.

- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

content.text: Let me set up a helper script for archive.org search and djvu availability checks, then run the top-priority references.

input.command:
S=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-sfmqrb-git-rishe/b3fc9033-a4ae-4052-ab02-8a5f609ee6da/scratchpad; mkdir -p $S/refs; cat > $S/ia.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: ia.sh "<query>" [rows]
q="$1"; rows="${2:-15}"
curl -s -G 'https://archive.org/advancedsearch.php' --data-urlencode "q=$q" --data-urlencode 'fl[]=identifier' --data-urlencode 'fl[]=title' --data-urlencode 'fl[]=year' --data-urlencode 'fl[]=access-restricted-item' --data-urlencode "rows=$rows" --data-urlencode 'output=json' | python3 -c '
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
for r in d["response"]["docs"]:
    print(r.get("identifier"),"|",r.get("year"),"|",r.get("access-restricted-item"),"|",str(r.get("title"))[:90])
'
EOF
cat > $S/djvu.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: djvu.sh <identifier>  -> prints djvu txt file name, size, HTTP status
id="$1"
f=$(curl -s "https://archive.org/metadata/$id" | python3 -c '
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
for f in d.get("files",[]):
    if f["name"].endswith("_djvu.txt"): print(f["name"], f.get("size"))
')
echo "$id -> $f"
name=$(echo "$f" | head -1 | cut -d" " -f1)
[ -n "$name" ] && curl -sIL "https://archive.org/download/$id/$name" | grep -i '^HTTP' | tail -1
EOF
chmod +x $S/ia.sh $S/djvu.sh
echo "== AHD"; $S/ia.sh 'title:(american heritage dictionary) AND mediatype:texts' 20
echo "== POK"; $S/ia.sh 'pokorny indogermanisches etymologisches AND mediatype:texts' 15
echo "== KLN"; $S/ia.sh 'klein comprehensive etymological dictionary english AND mediatype:texts' 15
echo "== HRN"; $S/ia.sh 'horn grundriss neupersischen etymologie AND mediatype:texts' 10
echo "== IEC"; $S/ia.sh 'mann indo-european comparative dictionary AND mediatype:texts' 10
echo "== KNT"; $S/ia.sh 'kent old persian grammar texts lexicon AND mediatype:texts' 10
echo "== SYN"; $S/ia.sh 'buck dictionary of selected synonyms indo-european AND mediatype:texts' 10

cat > $S/pageoff.py <<'EOF'
import sys,re,collections
# usage: pageoff.py file  -> prints number of ff pages, most common (ffindex - printed) offsets, and sample
txt=open(sys.argv[1],encoding='utf-8',errors='replace').read()
pages=txt.split('\f')
print("ff pages:",len(pages), "chars:",len(txt))
offs=collections.Counter(); samples={}
for i,p in enumerate(pages):
    lines=[l.strip() for l in p.strip().split('\n') if l.strip()]
    cand=lines[:3]+lines[-3:]
    for l in cand:
        m=re.fullmatch(r'[—\-–\s]*(\d{1,4})[—\-–\s]*',l)
        if not m:
            m=re.match(r'^(\d{1,4})\s+\S',l) or re.search(r'\S\s+(\d{1,4})$',l)
        if m:
            n=int(m.group(1))
            if 0<n<3000:
                offs[i-n]+=1
                samples.setdefault(i-n,(i,n,l[:60]))
for o,c in offs.most_common(6):
    print(f"offset ff-printed={o}: {c} hits, e.g. ffpage {samples[o][0]} printed {samples[o][1]} line {samples[o][2]!r}")
EOF
cd $S/refs; for f in AHD_watkins1985 POK_01 POK_02 POK_03 POK_full KLN_1966 KLN_1971 HRN IEC KNT SYN; do echo "=== $f"; python3 $S/pageoff.py $f.txt; done

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""usage: paginate.py <identifier> <out.txt> [basename-filter]
Builds a local text with \f between leaves (leaf i == ff-page i, 0-based) from IA hocr_searchtext+pageindex,
falling back to djvu.xml. Prints page_numbers-derived offset."""
import sys,json,gzip,io,re,collections,urllib.request,urllib.parse,html
ident,out=sys.argv[1],sys.argv[2]; filt=sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv)>3 else ''
meta=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f'https://archive.org/metadata/{ident}'))
names=[f['name'] for f in meta['files'] if filt in f['name']]
def get(name):
    u=f'https://archive.org/download/{ident}/'+urllib.parse.quote(name)
    r=urllib.request.urlopen(u,timeout=300); data=r.read()
    if name.endswith('.gz'): data=gzip.decompress(data)
    return data
pi=[n for n in names if n.endswith('_hocr_pageindex.json.gz')]
st=[n for n in names if n.endswith('_hocr_searchtext.txt.gz')]
pages=[]
if pi and st:
    idx=json.loads(get(pi[0])); txt=get(st[0])
    for e in idx:
        pages.append(txt[e[0]:e[1]].decode('utf-8','replace'))
    src='hocr'
else:
    xmls=[n for n in names if n.endswith('_djvu.xml')]
    if not xmls: print('NO SOURCE',names); sys.exit(1)
    data=get(xmls[0]).decode('utf-8','replace')
    for obj in re.split(r'<OBJECT\b',data)[1:]:
        lines=[]
        for ln in re.findall(r'<LINE>(.*?)</LINE>',obj,re.S):
            words=re.findall(r'<WORD[^>]*>(.*?)</WORD>',ln,re.S)
            lines.append(html.unescape(' '.join(words)))
        pages.append('\n'.join(lines))
    src='djvuxml'
open(out,'w',encoding='utf-8').write('\f'.join(pages))
print(f'{ident}: {len(pages)} leaves written to {out} via {src}, {sum(len(p) for p in pages)} chars')
pn=[n for n in names if n.endswith('_page_numbers.json')]
if pn:
    d=json.loads(get(pn[0]))
    offs=collections.Counter(); ex={}
    for p in d['pages']:
        s=p.get('pageNumber') or ''
        if s.isdigit():
            o=p['leafNum']-int(s); offs[o]+=1; ex.setdefault(o,(p['leafNum'],int(s)))
    for o,c in offs.most_common(4):
        print(f'  page_numbers: leaf = printed + {o}  ({c} leaves, e.g. leaf {ex[o][0]} = p.{ex[o][1]})')
    nums=[int(p['pageNumber']) for p in d['pages'] if (p.get('pageNumber') or '').isdigit()]
    if nums: print(f'  printed range {min(nums)}-{max(nums)}')
EOF
